eras.label: Pre-Islamic (~600 CE)
eras.note: Majority Christian — Coptic Orthodox was the faith of virtually all Egyptians. Jewish community in Alexandria was one of the largest in the world. Small pagan and Gnostic communities.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: Alexandria was a major Jewish center

eras.label: 1927 Census (British era)
eras.note: First modern census with religious breakdown. Christians ~8% after 1,300 years of gradual conversion to Islam.

eras.label: Today (2024)
eras.note: Christians grew in absolute numbers but fell as share of population. Jewish community effectively extinct.

eras.label: Ancient / Carthaginian era (~200 BCE)
eras.note: Berber-Punic civilization. Later Roman province — Christianity arrived by 2nd century CE. Large Jewish community predating Islam by 600+ years.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: Ancient community — predates Islam by centuries

groups.name: Early Christian
groups.note: Tertullian, Augustine born in North Africa

eras.label: 1956 (Independence)
eras.note: French rule ends. ~300,000 European Catholics and 100,000 Jews depart within a decade.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: ~100,000 — majority emigrated to Israel and France

groups.name: Christian
groups.note: Mostly foreign workers and sub-Saharan migrants

eras.label: Late Roman era (~400 CE)
eras.note: North Africa was Christian majority. St. Augustine was Bishop of Hippo (modern Annaba, Algeria). Berber-Jewish communities predating Christianity.

eras.label: 1962 (Independence)
eras.note: French colonial period ends. Near-total exodus of Europeans and Jews within 2 years.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: ~140,000 — all held French citizenship, all left

eras.label: Pre-Islamic (~600 CE)
eras.note: Berber majority with significant Jewish communities — some of the oldest in North Africa. Roman-era Christian communities in northern Morocco.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: ~265,000 — largest Jewish community in Arab world

eras.label: Byzantine era (~500 CE)
eras.note: Christian majority under Byzantine Empire. Jewish communities in Cyrenaica (eastern Libya) for over 1,000 years. Berber-Jewish culture in western Libya.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: Cyrenaica Jewish community documented since 100 BCE

eras.label: Byzantine era (~600 CE)
eras.note: Syria was the heart of Eastern Christianity. Antioch was the third most important city in the Roman Empire. Large Jewish communities in Antioch, Damascus, Aleppo.

groups.name: Christian (Byzantine/Syriac)
groups.note: Antioch — where disciples were first called Christians

eras.label: Byzantine / Early Islamic (~700 CE)
eras.note: Mount Lebanon was a stronghold of Maronite Christianity. Druze faith emerged here in the 11th century. Jewish communities in coastal cities.

eras.label: 1932 French census
eras.note: Last official census. Christians ~54% — basis for constitutional power-sharing that still governs Lebanon today.

eras.label: Today (~2024 estimates)
eras.note: No census since 1932. All figures are estimates. Palestinian and Syrian refugees (mostly Sunni/Shia) have changed demographics significantly.

eras.label: Sassanid / Pre-Islamic (~600 CE)
eras.note: Mesopotamia was religiously diverse. Jewish community in Babylon was the largest in the world — center of Jewish learning (Babylonian Talmud compiled here). Large Christian population. Zoroastrian majority in elite class.

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: Largest Jewish community in the world — Babylonian Talmud compiled here

eras.label: 1947 census
eras.note: 12% Christian. 40% of Baghdad was Jewish before 1948.

eras.label: Sassanid Empire (~600 CE)
eras.note: Zoroastrianism was the state religion — majority faith for over 1,000 years before Islam. Large Jewish community in Persia since the Babylonian exile (586 BCE).

groups.name: Jewish
groups.note: Present since Babylonian exile 586 BCE — Cyrus freed them

eras.label: Today (2024)
eras.note: Official figures show 95% Muslim. Independent GAMAAN surveys (2020–23) suggest significant irreligion — up to 30% may be non-practicing or atheist.

groups.name: Shia Muslim (official)
groups.note: GAMAAN surveys suggest practicing rate may be ~40%

groups.name: Irreligious / atheist
groups.note: GAMAAN estimates 15–30%; state does not recognize

eras.label: Byzantine era (~1000 CE)
eras.note: Anatolia was the heartland of Byzantine Christianity. Constantinople was the most important Christian city in the world. Large Greek, Armenian, and Syriac communities.

eras.label: Gandharan Buddhist era (~700 CE)
eras.note: Afghanistan was the crossroads of the ancient world — Buddhist, Zoroastrian, Hindu, and early Islamic communities coexisted. Bamiyan Buddhas carved 500–650 CE. Silk Road brought traders of every faith.

eras.label: Pre-partition / Indus Valley (~1900 CE)
eras.note: The region of modern Pakistan was religiously diverse under British India. Lahore, Karachi, and Peshawar had significant Hindu, Sikh, and Muslim populations living together.

eras.label: 1947 (Partition)
eras.note: 14 million people displaced in largest mass migration in history. Hindus and Sikhs fled west; Muslims fled east. Violence killed 200,000–2,000,000.

eras.label: Pre-colonial (~1800 CE)
eras.note: The region had diverse religious traditions. The Sokoto Caliphate dominated the north after Usman dan Fodio's 1804 jihad. The south was predominantly animist/traditional with some Christian missionaries arriving from the 1840s.

eras.label: 1963 census (last official religious count)
eras.note: Nigeria has deliberately not published religious census data since 1963 — the north/south split is too politically explosive.

eras.label: Today (~2024 estimates)
eras.note: No official religious census since 1963. All figures are estimates. Northern states ~96% Muslim. Southern/eastern states ~80% Christian.

groups.name: Muslim
groups.note: Northern states 12 of which have full sharia law

eras.label: Nubian Christian kingdoms (~900 CE)
eras.note: Sudan had three Christian kingdoms — Nobatia, Makuria, and Alodia — that survived the Arab conquest and maintained Christianity for 600 years after Egypt became Muslim. The last Christian Nubian king converted to Islam in 1315.

eras.label: 1956 (Independence)
eras.note: Before South Sudan's 2011 secession, Sudan had a large Christian and animist south.

eras.label: Today (2024)
eras.note: After South Sudan's independence in 2011, Sudan lost ~6M Christians. Remaining Christians face civil war.

eras.label: Aksumite Empire (~400 CE)
eras.note: Ethiopia was the second country in the world (after Armenia) to adopt Christianity as a state religion — in 330 CE. The Beta Israel Jewish community has been present for at least 1,500 years.

eras.label: Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms (~1000 CE)
eras.note: The Indonesian archipelago was dominated by Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms — Majapahit (Hindu), Srivijaya (Buddhist). Islam arrived via Arab and Indian traders from the 13th century onward.

eras.label: 1965 (Independence / Pancasila enacted)
eras.note: Blasphemy law enacted recognizing only 6 religions. Communist purge kills 500,000–1M, many of whom were Chinese Buddhists/Confucians.

eras.label: Buddhist era (~1100 CE)
eras.note: The Maldives was Buddhist for over 1,500 years. Buddhist temples, stupas, and monasteries documented across the islands. A unique Indian Ocean Buddhist civilization.

eras.label: 1153 CE (The conversion)
eras.note: Sultan Dhovemi converts to Islam and orders the entire population to follow. Within one generation, Buddhism is extinct on every island. The most complete religious conversion in recorded history.

eras.label: Today (2024)
eras.note: Constitution Article 9(d): Non-Muslims cannot be citizens. The most legally complete religious uniformity of any country on earth.

groups.name: Sunni Muslim
groups.note: Legally required for citizenship — non-Muslim citizenship constitutionally impossible

groups.name: Christian converts (underground)
groups.note: Estimated dozens to low hundreds — face imprisonment
